title: Houthis seize the Galaxy Leader cargo ship in the Red Sea
body:
On 19 November 2023, Yemen's Houthi movement seized the vehicle carrier Galaxy Leader in the Red Sea, about 150 kilometres off the Yemeni port of Hodeida, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre. US defense officials confirmed the seizure and said the Houthi fighters reportedly rappelled onto the ship from a helicopter. The Bahamas-flagged ship was sailing from Korfez in Turkey to Pipavav in India and had its AIS tracker switched off.

Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for the seizure of what he called an Israeli ship. The Israel Defense Forces said it was not an Israeli ship and that the crew was international and civilian. The Prime Minister's Office said 25 crew members from Ukraine, Bulgaria, the Philippines and Mexico were aboard. The vessel was registered to a British company partially owned by Israeli businessman Abraham Ungar and leased to a Japanese company.

Israel's Prime Minister's Office called the incident another act of Iranian terrorism and said it was carried out on an Iranian whim. The Houthis had pledged to target ships linked to Israel and had fired missiles and drones toward Eilat since the start of the war. The seizure was the first of a series of Houthi attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea, which prompted a US-led maritime security initiative announced in December 2023.
